title: Optimize / Evals 1:1 prep - quality regressions & A/B check
content:
Goal for 1:1
- Quick sync with Samir / Aisha to align on next steps for the recent quality regression seen in the latest A/B.
- Come with concrete action items (who/what/when) so we can move to canary or rollback quickly.

Background / quick summary
- Eval harness: opt-eval-v2 (prod-sampled queries, stratified by route).
- Sample size: 10k production queries from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-16.
- Variants: control = model v1.3 (baseline, full precision), experiment = model v1.4-quant (weight-quant + prompt-template change).
- Observed regression: preference score down ~3.4 pts (control 67.2 -> experiment 63.8). Hallucination rate up (2.1% -> 4.8%). Task-specific F1 for KB retrieval down 3.6 pts.
- A/B config: 50/50 offline eval + small online 1% split for initial safety checks. Online signaling shows early signs of user friction on the KB route (increased requery and clarified prompts).

What I want to cover in the meeting
1) Confirm metric signal is real (Samir): checks to run now
   - Re-run opt-eval-v2 with fixed seed and same prompt set (billing-qa-prompts & kb-retrieval) to confirm reproducibility.
   - Compare token-level diffs for a 200-case failure set to understand hallucination patterns.
2) Prompt drift / template change review (Aisha):
   - Walk through the prompt-template changes applied in v1.4 (shortening anchor text + new system message).
   - Quick manual inspect of 20 high-impact failures to see if template caused brevity that triggers hallucination.
3) Telemetry and alerting (Lena / SRE):
   - Ensure dashboard shows per-route hallucination rate and requery rate; set temporary alert at +1.5x baseline.
4) Canary / rollout decision tree (us):
   - Options: roll back v1.4 everywhere; patch prompt template and redeploy to canary 5%; continue controlled canary but restrict to non-KB routes.

Immediate hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: Quantization introduced subtle distributional changes that increase hallucination on long-context KB retrieval prompts.
- Hypothesis B: Prompt-template change shortened the system framing and removed an anchor instruction that prevented hallucination in edge cases.
- Hypothesis C: Combined effect (quantization + prompt) crosses threshold where cache/batching interacts badly for some seq lengths.

Quick checks to run before 1:1 (low latency)
- Samir: kick a re-run of opt-eval-v2 focused on the failing prompt set (billing-qa-prompts + kb-retrieval) with both float and quant weights (due by EOD local).
- Aisha: produce a diffed sample of 50 failed examples with before/after outputs and label type (hallucination, omission, formatting) - share in thread.
- Lena: enable per-route telemetry for hallucination and requery for next 24h and provide a short dashboard link.

Agenda (15-20m)
- 2m: quick recap of numbers (I’ll present).
- 6m: Samir shows re-run results / reproducibility.
- 5m: Aisha shows prompt diffs + manual failure cases.
- 3m: decide immediate action (rollback vs patch + canary) and assign action items.

Proposed decision thresholds (suggested)
- If hallucination rate > +2x baseline on KB route and preference drop > 3 pts => immediate rollback to v1.3 for all KB-serving routes.
- If signal is < threshold or only in narrow prompt set => patch prompt + 5% canary restricted to non-critical customers for 24-48h.

Action items (put on the record for the 1:1)
- Samir: Re-run opt-eval-v2 focused tests and produce reproducibility note + short report (due 2026-03-20 EOD).
- Aisha: Produce 50-case failure sample with labels and highlight where prompt anchors missing (due 2026-03-20 noon).
- Lena: Enable / verify telemetry and create temporary alert; share dashboard link (due 2026-03-20 15:00).
- Jamie (me): Draft rollback playbook and canary config (5% traffic, exclude KB route) for review (due 2026-03-20 18:00).
- Samir + Aisha: If prompt patch candidate exists, run small offline AB (control vs prompt-patch) on 2k examples and surface metrics (due 2026-03-22).

Notes to ask in 1:1
- How much of the regression is concentrated in top-10 prompt templates? (if concentrated, narrow patching).
- Any infra constraints for rolling back quantized weights quickly? (time to rollback, deployment windows).
- Customer impact: do we have any support tickets / CS escalations referencing hallucinations since 2026-03-11? (if yes, escalate to CS).

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- We need to confirm if batching/kv-cache behavior changes under quantized runtime affect long-context attention. If yes, SRE + serving-runtime team sync required.
- Should add unit/regression tests that run a small set of anchor prompts against any model build that changes template or quantization.

Back-of-envelope risk assessment
- Rollback cost: low (we have tested rollback scripts) but costs dev time and few minutes of customer traffic flicker.
- Patch + canary cost: medium (needs quick turnaround on prompt engineer + extra monitoring).
- Leave as-is: high risk (customer-facing regression could get worse; not acceptable).

Slack / links to share in meeting
- Eval results: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/opt-eval-v2-results
- PR with quant changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/412
- Jira ticket: OPT-678

Quick personal notes (jamie)
- Ask Samir if re-run uses exact same tokenization / detokenization pipeline (we've seen differences sneak in there).
- If Aisha confirms anchor missing, propose adding an explicit guard line to system message: "Do not fabricate facts; if uncertain, say 'I don't know' and ask to clarify."

Post-meeting deliverables
- Update confluence note with decision + short rationale and selected mitigation path.
- Create follow-up thread with labeled failure examples and plan for permanent regression test.

-- end --
